foreverChanges.title: Hit and Crit are unified — including poisons
foreverChanges.body: Spell, melee and ranged hit chance are combined into one stat, and the same happens to critical chance. Blizzard named Rogues directly: the change "helps hybrid specializations such as Retribution Paladins and Enhancement Shaman, while also letting Warriors, Hunters, and Rogues benefit when improving the reliability of tools such as Taunts, Poisons, and Traps."
foreverChanges.impact: Your gear no longer has dead stats on it, and your poison applications stop living on a separate table from your swings.

foreverChanges.title: Weapon Skill survives, but tuned down per item
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard's own wording: "Weapon skill still works as it always has, but items with weapon skill offer less of it per item so they are not always the obvious best choice."
foreverChanges.impact: Still cap your weapon skill. Do not expect one item to do half the job for you the way a couple of Classic pieces did.

foreverChanges.title: New stat: fewer parries and dodges
foreverChanges.body: Among the reworked and added stats, Blizzard says "some items can reduce the chance for attacks to be parried or dodged."
foreverChanges.impact: A new line to weigh on melee gear. How much it is worth against Hit and Agility is a question for sims, not guesswork. Anything attacking a boss from the front has the most to gain.

foreverChanges.title: Itemization is being deliberately "unsolved"
foreverChanges.body: Every dungeon drop has been re-examined and hundreds of new drops added. Unique dungeon boss items are now blue quality, set bonuses are improved, quest rewards support more classes and roles, world-drop epics are improved, there are hundreds of new rare-creature drops and over 600 new profession recipes. Some new effects tie items to environments (Woodlands, Mountains, Deserts) or creature types, and trinkets lean toward situational effects.
foreverChanges.impact: Do not build a Forever BiS list from Classic Era data. It will be wrong, and confidently wrong is worse than empty.

foreverChanges.title: Talent trees keep their shape, not all their talents
foreverChanges.body: Trees keep a familiar structure and the same number of rows, with one-point milestone talents at 11, 21 and 31 points joined by a new 16-point milestone. Blizzard says some talents remain exactly as they were in patch 1.12, some have been adjusted or improved, and key class-buff talents become baseline.
foreverChanges.impact: Every talent split on this page is a Classic Era build. Blizzard has not published the Forever Rogue trees, so treat them as provisional.

foreverChanges.title: Slower, more tactical combat
foreverChanges.body: Combat stays rooted in Classic pacing: "A solo player can expect an ordinary creature to take roughly 10–15 seconds to defeat." Crowd control keeps its place, damage dealers "still need to respect Threat," and classes are meant to stay simple and distinct, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
foreverChanges.impact: Sap, Kick, Blind and Gouge stop being things you forgot you had, and threat management is part of the job.

foreverChanges.title: Skyborne can be Rogues
foreverChanges.body: Both Skyborne factions, Windshaper (Horde) and High Order (Alliance), can be Rogues. Shared racials: Walk on Air (glide downward for 10 seconds), Wind Blessed (passive 1% melee, ranged and spell Haste) and Elemental Insight (5% more damage to Elementals). Windshaper adds Skysight (10% run speed); High Order adds Read Ley Line (100% more Health and Mana regeneration). The race requires the Skyborne Heroic Pack or higher.
foreverChanges.impact: A flat 1% Haste is the headline for a melee class, and there is nothing like it on the Classic racial list. Whether it beats Human or Orc weapon racials is a sim question.

foreverChanges.title: Account-wide Legacy System
foreverChanges.body: A horizontal progression system built from Legacy Challenges, Perks and Rewards. Most players unlock it when their first character reaches level 25, and at launch each character can spend up to 16 Legacy Points. Perks are quality-of-life and efficiency boosts, not combat power. One, Working Overtime, raises skill-up chances in every tradeskill, including Lockpicking.
foreverChanges.impact: Your alts and your main share progress. None of it changes your damage, but Lockpicking gets easier to level.

foreverChanges.title: Raid and dungeon lineup
foreverChanges.body: Two raids: Hyjal Summit (20-player) and Barrow Deeps (10-player). Nine dungeons: Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Whelgar's Excavation Site, City of Dalaran, Blackmaw Hold, Drowned City, Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison and Shaper's Terrace. New zones Mount Hyjal, Shen'dralas, Riverglades and the Skyborne starting zone Zephras Isle, plus Darkspear Islands, a 15v15 battleground.
foreverChanges.impact: Names and counts are locked in, but encounter mechanics and loot tables are not. The raid notes on this page are still Classic Era tiers until real Forever strats exist.

foreverChanges.title: Beta: what is open
foreverChanges.body: The beta opened September 17th with a level cap of 20, to be raised to 30 later in the test. Week one covered the Skyborne race and Zephras Isle, all zone content up to level 20, and two dungeons: Hall of Thanes (13–18) and Ruins of Lordaeron (15–20). More zones, dungeons and the new battleground open as the beta continues, and October 21st is the last full day of testing. Beta access comes with the Skyborne Epic Pack or higher.
foreverChanges.impact: You can play a Forever Rogue now, just not far. Blizzard has not announced a date for the level 30 raise.

foreverChanges.title: Beta notes: the Rogue changes so far
foreverChanges.body: The September 24th development notes have one Rogue entry: "Sap now correctly flags the Rogue for PvP when used on a target that is PvP flagged." Talent resets are temporarily 1 silver for the beta. Two known issues affect Rogues: "Item enhancements (such as Windfury or rogue poisons) cannot be tracked" by the new Cooldown Manager, and "Personal Resource Display doesn't show combo points."
foreverChanges.impact: Rogue talent and tuning changes you see reported from the beta are not in Blizzard's published notes. Test them in the client rather than trusting a screenshot.

foreverChanges.title: Rogue class preview
foreverChanges.body: The Deep Dive went into Paladin changes ability by ability, but Blizzard has not published anything comparable for Rogue: no Rogue talent trees, spec direction, new abilities or weapon changes. Blizzard says more class and race detail is coming in future videos and articles.
foreverChanges.impact: Anything claiming a specific Forever Rogue rotation, spec identity or new ability is your own beta testing or someone else's guess. Trust the beta client over secondhand claims.

poisons.name: Instant Poison
poisons.note: Chance on hit for immediate damage. The default on both weapons for Combat, and it scales with how often you swing.

poisons.name: Deadly Poison
poisons.note: Stacking damage over time, five stacks maximum. Assassination’s off-hand answer — applies on the swing, ticks for free.

poisons.name: Wound Poison
poisons.note: Reduces healing received. Mostly a PvP tool, occasionally the right call on a healing add.

poisons.name: Crippling Poison
poisons.note: Movement slow. For kiting fixates and for PvP, never for your parse.

poisons.name: Mind-numbing Poison
poisons.note: Casting slow. Carry a few in case a caster add needs softening.

faqs.a: No. Poisons do not scale with Spell Power in Classic. The only place Spell Power touches a Rogue is Dragonbreath Chili, which is a curiosity for people chasing the last fraction of a percent. What does change in Forever: Blizzard confirmed the unified Hit stat covers every attack including poisons, so your hit rating will feed poison applications in a way it does not today.

Yes. Instant Poison and Deadly Poison damage both scale with your Attack Power — confirmed by a dev on the Rogue Classic Discord. It is not a huge chunk of the total, but it is real, and it is one more reason a Rogue stacking Attack Power sees it show up everywhere on the damage meter, not just in white swings.

faqs.q: What has Blizzard actually confirmed for Rogues in Forever?
faqs.a: Three things, concretely. Rogues can use One-Handed Axes. Each spec is getting a sharper identity — Assassination toward poison damage, Subtlety toward bleeds and stealth, Combat staying upfront. And the talent trees keep their Classic shape while individual talents are redesigned around a new 16-point milestone. Mutilate appeared on the Assassination tree in the BlizzCon demo, but that is community capture from playable footage, not a published ability. Blizzard has published a full ability-by-ability rework preview for Paladin and has not yet done the same for Rogue.

faqs.q: How does unified Hit and Crit change my gearing?
faqs.a: It removes the dead stats. In Classic, spell hit on a piece of gear is worthless to you and melee hit is worthless to a Mage. In Forever there is one Hit stat and one Crit stat covering every attack a character makes. Blizzard’s worked example was Lionheart Helm — plus 18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit, all of it applying to everything. The practical effect for you is that more items become plausible, and fewer of them are obviously other people’s loot.

faqs.q: Should I build a Forever BiS list now?
faqs.a: No, and you should be suspicious of anyone who has. Blizzard has reviewed the loot on every dungeon boss and is updating quests, world drops, professions and existing items, with hundreds of new or adjusted drops and some effects tied to specific environments or creature types. The stated goal is to "unsolve" Classic. A Classic Era BiS list ported to Forever will be confidently wrong, which is worse than being empty.

leveling.name: Mutilate
leveling.body: Built entirely around Mutilate and your poisons. Every fight runs on Mutilate for fast combo points while poisons tick on everything you hit. Straightforward, hard-hitting, and at its best when you keep your poisons topped up.

leveling.name: Blade Flurry
leveling.body: Traditional Combat, centered on cleaving with Blade Flurry. Pull two or three mobs, turn on Blade Flurry and take them down together with the familiar Sinister Strike, Slice and Dice and Eviscerate loop. No positioning to worry about.

leveling.name: Improved Ambush
leveling.body: A Subtlety hybrid built around a devastating opener. Stealth in, open with a big Ambush and finish most mobs before they can fight back, then reset and move on. Quick kills, less downtime, and more picking your battles.

changelog.text: Fixed placeholder mail gear issue, updated level 30 talent builds, updated UI strings and preview. Still a lot of work to do, but getting there.
Stood up the first iteration of the WoW Forever Rogue Handbook — spec board, talents, poisons, rotation, gear, consumables and the Forever watch, all in one place.
Warcraft Forever announced at BlizzCon. Beta September 17th, launch November 4th, level cap staying at 60. Rogues confirmed to gain One-Handed Axes.
